title: A multi-purpose pilot-scale molten metal & molten salt pyrolysis reactor
author: Riedewald, Povey, et al.

steps.title: Check pilot plant leak‑tightness
steps.instruction: Inspect the pilot‑scale molten metal & molten salt pyrolysis reactor for leak‑tightness and overall performance using biomass (biodegradable plastic coffee lids) and carbon‑fibre feedstock before any target‑material experiments.

substeps.instruction: Prepare biodegradable plastic coffee lids as biomass feedstock.
Prepare carbon‑fibre resin as a second feedstock.
Run the reactor under normal operating conditions.
Observe the system for any leaks or abnormal pressure changes.

steps.title: Test system with coffee lids
steps.instruction: Run a pyrolysis experiment using biodegradable plastic coffee lids; collect the condensate (bio‑oil) and verify that the amount matches literature values, confirming both leak‑tightness and condenser functionality.

substeps.instruction: Load the coffee lids into the reactor.
Heat the reactor to the required pyrolysis temperature (as used in the study).
Collect the condensate in the designated collection vessel.
Compare the volume of bio‑oil obtained with the values reported in reference [20].

steps.title: Pyrolyse carbon‑fibre resin
steps.instruction: Perform a pyrolysis run with carbon‑fibre resin, using a 100 mL condensate collection vessel; note that no water is collected and that the heat‑transfer salt remains dry after a weekend idle period.

substeps.instruction: Load carbon‑fibre resin into the reactor.
Run the pyrolysis under the same conditions as the biomass test.
Collect condensate in a 100 mL vessel.
Confirm that the condensate contains no water.
Verify that the heat‑transfer salt stays dry after the reactor has been idle over a weekend.

steps.title: Inspect vapour with interceptor vessel
steps.instruction: Install an interceptor vessel downstream of the condenser to visually inspect the vapour stream during a beechwood biomass pyrolysis; observe suspended wax droplets and note brown deposits on the glass when the vessel is not cleaned between runs.

substeps.instruction: Install the interceptor vessel in the vapour line after the condenser.
Run a pyrolysis experiment using beechwood as feedstock.
Visually inspect the vapour for tiny wax droplets suspended in the stream.
If the vessel is not cleaned between experiments, record the appearance of brown deposits on the glass surface.

steps.title: Recover floating biochar from solidified tin
steps.instruction: After pyrolysis of biodegradable plastics, carbon fibre, or beechwood on molten tin, allow the tin to solidify; remove the solidified tin and recover the floating biochar (or other carbon/SiO₂ residues) without loss of tin.

substeps.instruction: Cool the reactor until the molten tin solidifies.
Extract the solidified tin block from the reactor.
Separate and collect the intact biochar or carbon/SiO₂ residues that floated on the tin.

steps.title: Pyrolyse printed circuit boards
steps.instruction: Place printed circuit boards (PCBs) in the reactor, perform pyrolysis on molten tin, and after cooling recover the PCB; note that no PCB metals dissolve in the tin because a carbon/glass‑fibre layer prevents contact.

substeps.instruction: Load the PCB into the reactor.
Run the pyrolysis under the same molten‑tin conditions used for the other materials.
Cool the reactor and solidify the tin.
Open the reactor and retrieve the treated PCB.
Observe that no PCB metals have dissolved into the tin.
